done_well_heading: Done correctly, as customary practice calls for
status: draft - warm wording for Cory to review; follows docs/expert/VOICE_RULE.md. {placeholders} are filled by code from the report's own words.
have_record: You said you received this record with the report. Please upload it, and it can answer this without asking the inspector.
not_performed: The report says this wasn't done: {topic}. Ask: What was the reason, and does it change what the report concludes?
not_checked: I couldn't check this part of the report: {detail} Ask the person who sent it for the original file.

air_without_outdoor_comparison.text: Air samples are reported without an outdoor comparison taken at the same time. Ask: Was an outdoor sample collected?
air_without_outdoor_comparison.why: Indoor results are read against what was outside at the time.

enclosed_air_read_as_room_air.text: A sample from inside a wall, cabinet or other enclosed space seems to be read as room air. Ask: How should that result be read?
enclosed_air_read_as_room_air.why: Air in an enclosed space is not the air people breathe in the room.

firmer_than_evidence.text: A conclusion is stated more firmly than the readings or samples shown. Ask: What makes it firm rather than possible?
firmer_than_evidence.why: The strength of a statement should match what supports it.

health_statement.text: The report makes a statement about health effects. Ask: What is it based on?
health_statement.why: Health statements need their own basis, apart from the building findings.

number_used_as_standard.text: A number is used like a safe or unsafe limit. Ask: What published standard is it taken from?
number_used_as_standard.why: There are no general safe or unsafe spore counts, so a limit needs a named source.

reading_without_dry_standard.text: Moisture readings are given without a dry reference. Ask: What were they compared to?
reading_without_dry_standard.why: A reading means little without a dry reading from a like material.

recommendation_without_support.text: A recommendation doesn't point to the reading, sample or observation behind it. Ask: What supports it?
recommendation_without_support.why: Each recommendation should trace to something in the report.

surface_sample_without_control.text: A surface sample is reported without a comparison from a clean, like surface. Ask: Was one taken?
surface_sample_without_control.why: A surface result is easier to read next to a clean comparison.

thermal_without_meter.text: Thermal imaging is used to suggest moisture without a meter reading confirming it. Ask: Was it confirmed with a meter?
thermal_without_meter.why: Thermal images show temperature differences, so a meter confirms moisture.

remediation_on_samples_alone.text: The recommended work rests on sample results, and the report shows no visual findings or moisture readings. Ask: What did the on-site inspection find that shows this work is needed beyond the lab result?
remediation_on_samples_alone.why: Lab results are one piece. What was seen and measured on site shows whether and where work is needed.

treatment_without_removal.text: The recommended work relies on treatment. Ask: How will growth and contaminated material be physically removed and checked?
treatment_without_removal.why: Removal is the usual first step, ahead of fogging, spraying or coatings.

value_under_other_location.text: A value appears under a different location than the one it describes. Ask: Which location does it belong to?
value_under_other_location.why: Each value should sit with its own location.

wet_without_reading.text: Something is called wet or damp, but no reading is shown. Ask: What was measured, and where?
wet_without_reading.why: A wet or damp call is easier to rely on with a reading beside it.

dates_disagree.text: The report gives two different dates. Ask: Why was sampling on a different day than the inspection?
dates_disagree.why: Conditions can change between days, and results describe the day sampled.

referenced_not_supplied.text: The report points to an attached lab report, but it was not in the file you sent. Could you ask the inspector for the full lab report?
referenced_not_supplied.why: The lab pages are where the sample results and their details live.

two_lab_names.text: The report names more than one laboratory. Ask: Which lab analyzed which sample?
two_lab_names.why: Each result should trace to the lab that produced it.

defined_never_used.text: The report defines categories but doesn't say which one applies to any area. Ask: Which category does each area fall into?
defined_never_used.why: The categories only help if they are applied.

time_spans_differ.text: The report gives two different time spans for the same step. Ask: Which one applies?
time_spans_differ.why: A contractor will follow one, and the two lead to different waits.

result_contradicts_threshold.text: A result is labeled in a way that doesn't match the report's own line. Ask: Which is right, the label or the number?
result_contradicts_threshold.why: The label and the number should agree.

baseline_labeled_elevated.text: A reference reading is labeled elevated. Ask: Is it a baseline, or was it elevated?
baseline_labeled_elevated.why: A baseline is the comparison point for the rest.

narrative_material_without_reading.text: The report describes moisture on a material in a room, but the room's reading table doesn't list one. Ask: Was that material measured?
narrative_material_without_reading.why: A statement of moisture is easier to rely on with a reading beside it.

cover_count_vs_sections.text: The number of samples stated near the front doesn't match the number of sample sections found. Ask: Which is the correct count, and are any sections missing?
cover_count_vs_sections.why: The count and the sections should line up so nothing is left out.

confirmed_vs_needs_lab.text: One line says something was confirmed, and another line about the same place says it still needs laboratory results. Ask: What was confirmed, and by what?
confirmed_vs_needs_lab.why: Confirmation usually rests on a laboratory result or a clearly stated basis.

rating_without_reading.text: A rating is given for a spot with no reading beside it, though the report's own rule uses a number. Ask: What was the reading?
rating_without_reading.why: A rating that rests on a number is easier to follow with the number shown.

instrument_not_listed.text: An instrument is used in the findings but isn't in the report's equipment list. Ask: Was that instrument used, and can the list be updated?
instrument_not_listed.why: The equipment list should match what was used.

number_vs_standard.text: A sentence compares a number with its own limit, and the wording and the numbers don't seem to agree. Ask: Which is intended?
number_vs_standard.why: A comparison should read the same way in words and in numbers.

citation_without_edition.text: A standard is named without an edition or section. Ask: Which edition and section was followed?
citation_without_edition.why: Standards change over time, so the edition and section show exactly what was relied on.

recommendation_without_measure_or_sample.text: In {area}, the report recommends work but doesn't show a reading or sample for that area. Ask: What supports the recommendation there?
recommendation_without_measure_or_sample.why: Work that is opened up or removed should rest on something measured or sampled.

recommendation_on_samples_alone.text: In {area}, the recommended work rests on sample results, and no visual finding or reading is shown for that area. Ask: What did the on-site inspection find there that shows the work is needed?
recommendation_on_samples_alone.why: A sample result is one piece. What was seen and measured on site shows where the work belongs.

cause_without_measure.text: In {area}, the report states a cause but doesn't show a reading for that area. Ask: What measurement points to that cause?
cause_without_measure.why: A cause is easier to rely on with a reading behind it.

conclusion_without_anything_behind_it.text: In {area}, the report draws a conclusion but doesn't show what was seen, measured or sampled there. Ask: What was the conclusion based on?
conclusion_without_anything_behind_it.why: Each conclusion should trace back to something in the report.
